data.title: T-3029: set the Green Tree Tavern on its ground in 1835
data.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"kevinrhaas"} -->
_Requested by **Kevin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01XPwihxLZTCL4xqRww9mX5v?thread=cmsg_01XPwihxLZTCL4xqRww9mX5vWHzMq8AihGxPY8sWFS1xDh)_

Owner-reported bug (visible-progress exemption 1): "green tree tavern in 1835 is sunken, it needs to be on the ground".

## What was wrong (measured)
- `buildings.js` beds a building on the lowest ground under it, sampled on a 5 x 5 grid over the **mesh bounding box**. The box reaches out to the eaves and fills the empty corners beside a wing.
- The Green Tree's rear ell (form.rear_ell, T-0083) runs 4.5 m east of the footprint down the South Branch bank. The box corner beside the ell sat on ground at 0.09 m, the front door's ground is 0.99 m: **the inn stood 0.89 m sunk** (in-app: anchor 0.094, front-door ground 0.988).
- T-0141 seated the inn against the bank using the footprint polygon only, so the ell was never in that measurement.

## Fix
1. **Renderer** (`building-feet.js`, `buildings.js`): a structure is bedded on the ground under its **feet**, the triangle edges on the GLB contract's y = 0 plane, sampled every ≤1 m. A structure with no geometry on that plane keeps the old box grid. Feet are packed to a Float32Array after placement. `feetOf(id)` is exposed, and the smoke's "no building hovers" gate now measures at the feet (box corners remain the fallback). Measured offline over every master GLB: 1904 has 0 structures moving >2 cm, 1835 has 13 of 677 (Green Tree +0.33 m, Wolf Point Tavern +0.27 m, the rest ≤0.06 m), 1812 has 5 (≤0.14 m). GLB-CONTRACT.md is updated.
2. **Re-seat**: the renderer fix alone leaves the inn 0.57 m sunk, because the ell is on the bank's slope. The inn moves **5.80 m west** by T-0141's own rule, now with the ell included: the first seat, in 0.1 m steps, where every wall foot meets the ground within 0.10 m. That is the relief 95% of the 1835 town stands on (p95 0.107 m). The move is inside the record's 20 m working uncertainty, and the corner reading (Lake and West Water) is unchanged. The position note says so.
3. **What follows the inn**: the walk, yard goods (bench, barrels, wagons, shed), woodpile, sidecar and the `green_tree` stand all move 5.80 m. The frontage generator now refuses a walk on a wall a built rear ell stands against; the re-seat would otherwise have laid one through the wing. The smoke frontage stands move the same 5.80 m.
4. **West Water Street**: T-0768/T-1547's cut rule stops the street where the roadway clears the inn, so its end moves 3.17 m along the same bank segment to [-22.02, -97.44]. The track still clears the inn by 0.06 m and the ell by 0.04 m, and the reach north of Lake is still 0.00 m. The street note is updated.
   - The e1834 heightfield is re-graded (4 cells, ≤0.08 m, at the street end) and the terrain GLB is re-baked in-container with the bpy 4.5.3 wheel. **The same bake on clean dev reproduces dev's bytes exactly.**
   - The West Division plat/lot/yard/fence/flora layers that read the line are re-derived through `rederive.mjs --tail`. Six recon Canal-block roofs and the forks freight house shift 0–2.6 m, and lot depths on that frontage shrink about 1 m.
   - The covered-wagon terrain pins are re-qualified: neither stand is near a changed cell.

## Shots (before = dev, after = this branch, same stands relative to the inn)
Desktop 1280×800 and phone 390×780, front oblique, front door at eye level, and the ell from the bank. All six pairs are in the project's `green-tree-ground-T-3029/` folder. No page errors in any of the four runs.

## Gate
`./tools/check.sh` **PASS** (1045 steps) before the dev merge. A re-run after merging dev is in progress, and the smoke by parts runs next (renderer change → every part).

## Found, not fixed here
The yard generators read the footprint polygon, not the ell, so the Green Tree's woodpile sits inside its rear ell (hidden, and it was there before this change too). 10 structures in 1835 carry a built rear ell.

data.title: T-3000: 1801 Prairie's hooded dormers, deck cresting and finials, and flank stack from the Taylor photograph
data.body:
## T-3000 — 1801 Prairie's roof from the Taylor photograph

Piece 3 of T-2540. J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 print shows the Kimball house's mansard carrying tall hooded dormers, a rail of iron cresting round its deck with turned finials, and a tall stone stack on the 18th Street flank. The build had none of them. All read through T-2538's solved camera.

**What shipped**
- **Hooded dormer** (`mansard.dormers[].head: "hood"`, K01): a short stone face with a small light under a shelf, and over it a slated hood whose front narrows as it climbs and whose cheeks widen against the receding roof, as the print's do. Built as solids in the K05 union. One on each face the camera sees: the street face at v 3.0, the 18th Street face at u 16.7. Each light's centre lands within about 10 px of the print's.
- **Mansard deck dressing** (`mansard.deck`, new `generators/archetypes/k01_mansard_deck.py`):
  - the K10 kit's iron cresting round the curb, stretched to the print's 0.55 m (29 px against about 30);
  - a turned finial at every deck corner (2.2 m; 116 px against about 120);
  - a slated pyramid hood under the north-west corner's finial.
  The hood is laid as its own faces, not joined into the union, because it stands astride the deck's hip, and K05's roof graph reads the two hips as one.
- **Flank stack:** u 5.0, 1.2 m across, cap top 16.4 m (y 458-477 against 462). A per-stack `cap_proud_m`/`cap_depth_m` gives it the heavy cap.
- **Byte-identity:** every other K01 house (and the K12/K13/K16 assets that hash `k01_frontage.py`) re-emits byte-identical. 31 inputs hashes are restamped in the manifest; only 1801's master and web GLB change. `k01_mansard_deck.py` joins the K01 helper list in `mesh_inputs.py`.
- **Provenance:** sections, the cresting's pattern (the kit's, not the print's pierced panels) and the finials' turnings are reconstructed, recorded in L-kimball-1801-deck-cresting-3000. The match record's T-3000 difference is now fixed, with two new open ones.
- **Not here:** the print's curb stands about 35-50 px lower than the build's, and its front deck ends at x 1092 where the build's runs to 1187. So the cresting, corner hood and south finial follow the build's curb, not the print's. The queue was at its 140-line ceiling, so this went to **T-1890 as a finding** rather than a new ticket. No second tier of dormers and no pavilion stack appear in this print.

**Verification**
- `tools/check.sh` on the merged tree (dev at 64e83fcd0), in three parts under the 600 s cap: 349 + 349 + 348 steps, none red. The one red was the stale local tickets BOARD/tickets.json, which are generated and uncommitted; after `ticket.mjs board` it re-ran green alone. numpy/scipy were installed first.
- After the second merge (T-3030, Glessner only): `validate.py --stale` 914/914 fresh (after re-materializing this clone's untracked Glessner v4 outputs), liberties, source-use and changelog checks OK. The full gate runs in CI on this head.
- Smoke, by `smoke_budget.mjs --for-diff` (parts 1-15; capped at the scaffold leg plus one): desktop part 1 **SMOKE PASS** (95/0); mobile part 3 (390×780, the card and liberties) **SMOKE PASS** (107/0).

- **The trace tool's sheet `35w`** (`tools/trace_prairie_1904_footprints.py`), plus one new rule: a sliver drawn at the street within 1.5 m of the building behind it counts as that building's front. This handles 2007's stone strip, which the sheet cuts off from its house with a line. The traces of sheets 20, 28, 28x, 35 and 35x are still byte-identical (`--check`).
- **27 drafts, baked:**
  - 13 houses: the row of nine 3B stone-bayed brick houses from 2007 to 2027, the frame houses at 2107, 2111 and 2119, and 2115–2117 (two houses on one 1904 lot).

- **Small tool changes:** `draft_prairie_1904.py` now knows Indiana Avenue and E. 21st Street. A site row may now declare `function_confidence`, so the church's function is `inferred`. Second Presbyterian's record is unchanged.

- **The church has no 1904 source in the repo.** Its function and its presence in 1904 are `inferred` from the 1911 label and are never shown as attested. T-3014 (new) is to source it and refine it.

Their census rows are ruled `phase_unresolved` and **nothing is drafted on them**, so no house is invented.

data.title: T-3017: 1904 parkway elms grow as open-grown American elms; leaf cards cut to their leaves
data.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"kevinrhaas"} -->
_Requested by **Kevin** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01XPwihxLZTCL4xqRww9mX5v?thread=cmsg_01XPwihxLZTCL4xqRww9mX5v11E8tKusbyKtcmRytW56DG)_

## Why

Owner, 2026-10-22, with his dev screenshot and two photographs of living street elms: the newer trees "appear as fans of leaves and not branches with variation", and then "those ones from before weren't perfect, they had cut off trunks and limbs that hung in the air so dont over correct on that".

**Finding.** The parkway elm was `ARCH.ulmus_americana` (the timber elm): one straight bole running up as a leader with 3-6 scaffolds off its top, under a round crown. On the phone (no near level) and past 10 m on desktop every elm is the `mid` level, which drew every other leaf clump as one card of the massed-clump tile (leaf atlas tile 5), 1.5-2.6 m across. That tile is a fan of sprays radiating from its foot, so each crown was a few hundred fans.

## What changed (visible)

- **`ARCH.ulmus_americana_vase` + `growElm`** (tree-model.js), named by the parkway spec (`spec.arch`): clear bole to 24-41 % of H; 2-4 co-dominant stems that fork up to three more times (each stem's first fork climbs into the middle of the vase); every limb arches, steep at the fork and reaching out at its end, bowing down past the crown's reach instead of stopping at a wall; branches sweep out and down off the limbs' upper reach; twigs hang. Crown about 0.85 of H wide (0.70 before), so the two files meet over the roadway.
- **No floating wood or leaf**: every child starts on its parent's polyline, inside and no thicker than the parent; the dome's leaf grows on short twigs off the upper wood instead of floating shell points.

## T-3006: K01 rounds a corner; 1811 Prairie's entrance block now turns on 0.9 m, as the 1888 plate shows

This is piece 2 of T-2989. T-3005 re-read the plate and found that the entrance block's south corner (K01's 'north') is rounded, about 0.9 m in radius, and K01 could not build that. This PR adds the rounded corner to K01 and uses it on 1811.

### What
- **`round_corner` (new K01 record field)** takes `{"corner": "north" | "south", "radius_m"}`. It builds a quarter round tangent to the street front and to the side wall it turns into.
  - It is laid in the front's own stone and coursed on the front's own beds from grade: base, coping, belt and rock-faced walling.
  - Each stone is curved in facets of at most 7.5°, done by the new `Assembly.round_stone`. No course holds more than two stones, and joints are staggered from course to course.
  - The front and the side wall are cut away over the round's span up to the stone's top. The side wall's brick and its string course start at the round's tangent.
- **The corner's head.** The round's last course (7.89–8.30 m on 1811) is a dressed corbel that rises from the round out to the square. The moulded cornice, the eave and the coped gable therefore stand on the square corner as before.
  - The plate does not show the corner's head: the oriel's roof covers it, and the coped gable's edge rises straight over the round's far side.
  - So the corbel is written down as an invention, `L-k01-1811-round-corner-3006` in docs/LIBERTIES.md.
- **The corner downpipe** now stands on the round, about 50° round from the front (s 10.29 m, `proud_m` −0.368), where the plate's rod at x 505–510 px puts it.
  - `front_pipes` now accepts a pipe behind the front's plane, but only on a round, and only standing as far off the curve as a front pipe stands off the front.
- **Validation (`_round_corner`) refuses:**
  - a round with no stone front, or with `brick_above_m` or a frontispiece
  - a quoined or returned south corner
  - a radius outside 0.3–1.5 m, or more than a quarter of the front block's width or depth
  - an opening, a bay or a side belt on the round
  - a pipe that stands off nothing, is buried in the round, or stands behind the flat front
- **1811's record** gains `form.round_corner`, graded `inferred` and sourced to the plate. The match record gains a new difference, "the entrance block's south corner is ROUNDED", now **fixed**. The pipe and arcade entries carry the change. The verdict stays `differs`: the oriel (T-3007), the arcade (T-2991) and the return pipe (T-2997) are still open.

### What the plate's camera reads now
The round runs from the front's tangent at x ≈ 469 px to its far side at ≈ 518, against the plate's 470 and 515–520. The pipe lands at x ≈ 508 against 505–510. The side-by-side is regenerated (`docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/coleman_ames_house_1811_prairie/`).

## T-3004 — Glessner's as-built Light derivative "stale on dev after #1187"

**Finding: dev is not stale. The fault was in the local tree the ticket was filed from. The validator blamed the committed derivative, and that misled.**

### What I measured
- **Fresh dev (9ed45595c, #1187):** `recover_glessner_v4.py --materialize`, then `validate.py --all`: **PASS, 0 errors**. `recover_glessner_v4.py --check` and `measure_web_derivatives.py --gate` are green too.
- **Rebuilt from scratch:** `tools/web_derivatives.sh --out /tmp/… --only glessner_house__as_built_1887.glb` (the pinned producer: build-light, gltf-transform, KTX2 and meshopt) reproduces **both committed derivatives byte for byte**. Full is `28e2c438…` and light is `79aee0bf…`, the light matching the manifest's `web_lods.light.output_sha256`. Its receipt's `master_sha256` (`a998f3f2…`) and `recipe_sha256` (`35f096ee…`) match the manifest.
- **The ticket's two errors, reproduced exactly:** I wrote the three outputs from the pre-#1187 archive (`90191f60f`) over a fresh tree. `validate.py --stale` then prints `light derivative is stale against its version master` and `light derivative bytes differ from the producer record`, **FAIL 2 error(s)**.

### Why CI didn't see it
The three v4 GLBs are **untracked outputs** of the committed archive parts (T-1730). A pull that brings a repacked archive never refreshes a clone's existing copies. `publish.sh`, and therefore `check.sh`, materializes first and refuses divergent bytes with the right advice. `validate.py` run alone reads the leftovers against the new manifest and blames the derivative instead. CI clones fresh every time, so it always materializes the current archive and never sees this.

### What changed
- `tools/recover_glessner_v4.py`: a new `drift()` hashes the three outputs against the committed `manifest.json`, with no unpacking. It returns `{path: missing|divergent}`.
- `tools/validate.py` (`--stale`): drift is reported first as **one error naming the cause and the remedy**: delete the outputs and run `--materialize`, or `--pack` after a bake. With drift present it skips the light-derivative checks, which would only be measuring the leftovers. A fresh clone with no outputs gets the same remedy in place of "the record of a bake outlived its output".
- `tools/test_glessner_v4_package.py`: a self-test for divergent, missing, healed and an unreadable manifest.
- The recovery README now documents the case.
- No GLB, manifest or archive is touched; dev's committed derivatives were already right. "Rebuild the derivative" is therefore answered by the byte-for-byte rebuild above, not by a new commit of one.

### Visible progress
This run is **invisible**, and its entry says "Nothing you can see changed". The recent What's-New run is v2177 visible, v2176 invisible, v2175 visible, with T-2985 (visible) pending fold. That puts this run over the one-in-four cap. I took it anyway: it was the queue's next free ticket (slice 4/5; T-2996 was in review, and T-2854's sign-off can't pass until the stable-end items it lists are built). This misleading error had also already cost a run, in this ticket. None of the three exemptions covers it.

### What the re-read found (`docs/RESEARCH/glessner-coursing-T-2986/`)

## T-2900 — 1801 Prairie's east range finished on K01

**Visible:** from Prairie Avenue the Kimball house's 18th Street flank now ends in the small round corner turret J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph shows: a round shaft, eaves level with the range's, and a slate cone with a finial to about 12.7 m. Behind it, the east range runs the 1911 sheet's whole length (v 0 → 18.3) under one slate hip, where before it stopped at the gabled section's 6 m.

### Kit (two new pieces, held by `tools/test_k01_wing_past_host.py`, registered in check.sh)
- **A K01 wing longer than its host wall** (`past_host`): it still stands on ≥ 1.0 m of the host wall. Past the host it has a front wall of its own, with its lights clear inside those stretches. Its roof is cut only along the host, so its eaves run round the front.
- **A K08 corner turret** (`corner: left|right`) on a rear wing's wall: its ring sits 0–0.3 m inside the end wall's plane and never past it, and its centre may stand inside the wall. Its wall top is the wing's own, its cone is whole over the wing's roof (`cap_whole`), and nothing is closed behind it on the wall plane.
- `check_bay_kit.py`: a whole cap may reach behind the wall face, but only inside its eaves' circle.
- The other K01-family masters re-key **byte-identical** (`validate.py --stale`: 891 match, 0 stale).

### Image gate
`taylor_c1895_northwest.match.json` stays at `differs`:
- **East-turret difference → fixed.** Its eaves are within ~5 px of the print's and its cone's flare within 5–10 px at both edges.
- **East-range item → stays "not shown"**, with how it is now built (this camera can't see the south 12 m).
- **New open difference:** the turret's first-floor band and eave moulding, and a finial ~40 px taller in the print.

### Liberties
`L-kimball-1801-turret-2900`: the turret stands 1.1 m proud where the sheet draws its bump about 0.6 m out. At 0.6 m the render showed about half the shaft the print shows past the flank's end, and the photograph is the closer evidence. The range's hip along its length and every opening on its unseen faces are reconstructed. `L-kimball-1801-k01-2843` has a Revised line pointing here.

- `./tools/check.sh` on the merged tree: **CHECK PASS — 1042 steps, none red**. numpy is missing on this runner, so the 9 steps that need it stood on a banked reading; the only lines naming it in the log are tagged `self-test |`.

data.title: T-2994: 1736 Prairie's 18th Street flank — its three canted bays from the 1911 sheet, and the mansard's date argued
data.body:
## T-2994 — 1736 Prairie's 18th Street flank from the 1911 sheet

Split from **T-2962** (piece 3 of T-2935). This PR is piece 1. **T-2995** has the rest: the roof behind the mansard's curb, the rear behind the brick bay (the "service wing"), the closed faces and the coach house. The roof needs a K01 widening (the mansard is four-sided in the kit today), so it would not fit one run alongside this work.

### What the sheet says (re-read off the raster, not the trace's role rule)
The 18th Street wall has **three** projections, all drawn **canted** and about 0.85 m out. Positions are in the record's frame, from the trace's outline:

| | sheet | at the wall (u) | face (u) | built |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rear | yellow, frame | 3.37–6.01 | 3.94–5.36 | K08 canted bay, frame, one storey |
| middle | pink, brick | 9.42–12.75 | 9.93–12.21 | K08 canted bay, brick, two storeys to a flat top under the eave |
| front | yellow, frame | 15.97–19.17 | 16.48–18.51 | K08 canted bay, frame, one storey |

The earlier read called the front one a **side porch** (the trace's rule: frame and under 15 m² on a masonry house). The sheet draws it in solid lines, closed and canted like the rear one, not in a porch's dashes, so it is built as a frame bay. The two front south windows move from 19.4/21.6 to 20.2/22.0 so the front bay's junction does not cut one.

### The mansard's date (argued in the phase's `documented_range`)
- New text source: `glessner_blog_2020_07_early_history_prairie_iv`, the Glessner House Museum post the photograph already comes from. Its text was read 2026-10-22. It says the house was "completed in 1864" for Granville S. Ingraham, and its author thinks the mansard "may well have been a later addition."
- Nothing read here dates the mansard. For the 1904 phase the answer doesn't matter: the c. 1890 photograph shows it and the 1911 sheet draws its curb.
- The curb's extent is recorded on `roof_form`. The dashed line runs only along the front and the 18th Street flank back to the brick bay. None is drawn along the north wall or over the rear 9.9 m. That is T-2995's to build.
- The blog is cited on the date, not on `roof_form`. It supports a date, not geometry, and `measure_rights_derivation --gate` correctly refused it on a geometry-bearing attribute.

### Image gate
Re-rendered `mcbirney_c1890_photo` on the new GLB. The bays stand behind the front's south corner from that camera, so the side-by-side is unchanged and the verdict is back to `matches`, with the reason written on the record. Review render from 18th Street: `docs/RESEARCH/k01-1736-mcbirney-2933/south-flank-t2994.jpg`.

### Verification
- Baked `house_1736_prairie` (K01 emit + web derivative). `k01_emit --check`, `check_bay_kit --check` and `validate.py --all` are green, including `--stale`.
- **Full `tools/check.sh` did not fit:** it was killed at the 590 s foreground limit on this 4-core runner (rc 124). I ran the steps covering this diff in the foreground instead, all green: validate.py --all, image_gate, k01_contract, k01_emit, check_bay_kit, compile_scene --check, grade_structures, compile_liberties, jaunt_built_so_far, compile_jaunts, compile_source_use, measure_rights_derivation --gate, measure_research_spend, pinned_sources, check-changelog, changelog-entries. CI's `chicago-4d-check` runs the whole gate, and the merge waits on it.

data.body:
## T-2992 — 1904 `light` back inside its triangle ceiling from the air over the district

**What.** I found this while lapping #1180: `tools/qa_draft_t2982.mjs`'s `air` stand (1360,-3620 at 110 m) read **1,323,370** triangles at 390x780 `light`, over the 1,270,000 ceiling. The breach is on dev itself; T-2982's drafts are only 16,980 of those triangles. Hiding each group in turn shows the railway costs 247,401 of the total. Two things in `renderers/web/js/railway.js` caused it:

1. **The far rails had no reach.** The header says "past the tie reach a zone draws only the ground", but the update has drawn the three-face strips to the end of the yard at every tier since T-2478. They now stop at `REACH[level].ties`: 220 m at `light`, 480 at `balanced`, 650 at `full`. From the air that removes 61,416 triangles of rail that was 600 m or more away and under a fifth of a pixel wide.
2. **The lake-edge cap was one mesh 3 km long.** That kept it from ever falling outside the sun's ±120 m box, so it drew into the shadow map wherever the visitor stood. It is now cut into the ground's 40 m cells with `spatialBatchAsync`, the same way as the ground decals. The triangles are the same, so the picture is the same. At this stand it drops from 9,120 triangles to 108.

**No ceiling moved.** `light` is the floor tier, so the railway gives the triangles back instead.

**Tools.**
- `measure_detail_ceilings.mjs --district` reads 1904 at the air stand. The ticket asks for this instrument, and before this it only knew the 1835 stands.
- `qa_railway_reach_t2992.mjs` renders the same held frame with the far rails as dev drew them and as shipped, compares every pixel, and uses a no-rails control.

## Verification
| 390x780 `light` | dev | branch | ceiling |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| qa_draft_t2982 air | 1,323,370 | **1,252,942** | 1,270,000 |
| measure_detail_ceilings --district (walker pose) | 1,266,335 | **1,195,907** | 1,270,000 |
| trackside, looking north (also over on dev) | 1,274,635 | **1,209,703** | 1,270,000 |

- **Pixels changed:** 122 of 304,200 from the air (every rail on screen there is a far rail). From the yard looking north, 130 changed, against 19,633 that change when every rail is hidden. Looking south, 68 against 18,409.
- **`qa_draft_t2982.mjs` on the branch:** desktop `full` and mobile `light` both PASS at every stand, with no page error and no failed request.
- **Smoke part 14 (the railway's part, from `smoke_budget --for-diff`):** **mobile 140 passed, 0 failed, SMOKE PASS.** Desktop part 14 did not finish inside the 600 s foreground cap: 86 checks passed with no real failure, and the only FAIL is the "browser closed" line from that timeout.

I ran the steps that touch this diff directly instead: the parse check on the changed modules, `check_spatial_batch.mjs`, and `changelog-entries --check` and `--self-test`. All pass. The full gate is this PR's CI run of `chicago-4d-check`.

## T-2974: Glessner's Prairie front openings registered on the raised beds

T-2955 raised the granite string 0.20 ft. After that, two of the Prairie front's opening heights no longer sat on a bed. This PR read every Prairie aperture's sill and head on HABS sheet 6 against the string, then built two and ruled on the rest. The full readings are in `docs/RESEARCH/glessner-prairie-openings-T-2974/README.md`, and `read_openings.py` re-derives them from the committed scan.

**Built**
- **First-floor sills: 9.2 → 8.71 ft (bed 8).** Sheet 6 draws each light's outer sill line on its eighth joint. Measured from the door-head joint (7.50), the four sills fall at 8.65–8.75. HABS photo 16, scaled on its printed 0.00 and 24.30, gives about 8.7.
- **First-floor heads: 14.5 → 14.3 ft.** The heads are not set on a bed. The string's bed 15 (13.92) would make the lights 5.21 ft high. The sheet draws all four at 5.61–5.62 ft and the photo shows about 5.5. Each head therefore stands the sheet's 5.6 ft above its sill.
- **Basement grille heads: 4.7 → 4.54 ft (bed 4).** Sheet 6 draws them on its fourth joint (4.57–4.61 on the sheet's own scale). Sheet, string and sheet 5 agree to within 0.08 ft at that height.

**Ruled, not built**
- **Front door:** already on bed 7 (T-2971). Its header and fan belong to T-2972.
- **Porte-cochère head:** drawn on bed 6 (6.88 against 7.0). It is left to **T-2978** (claimed by a sibling, sheet-4 passage heights), so it isn't moved twice.
- **Small pair:** within 0.15 ft of the sheet, and above bed 8, where no bed can be read.
- **Second-floor sills:** the sheet reads about 19.2–19.4 against the record's 19.8. That is filed as **T-2985**, because fixing it moves T-2965's colonnettes.
- **The string above bed 7:** sheets 5 and 6 and photo 16 all draw the courses about 7 % taller than the printed inches. Filed as **T-2986**.

**Visible:** yes. The four first-floor windows drop 15 cm at the sill and 6 cm at the head, and the grille heads drop 5 cm.

**habs-16-prairie-front:** re-rendered and reviewed. Through its camera, the opening's height is 95 px against the plate's 94.5 (90 before), and sill above grille head is 77.5 px against 75.5 (83 before). A uniform 8–10 px vertical offset on every feature comes from the camera's reconstructed height. The verdict stays `differs` because course relief is still open.

Group of two tickets on 1811 Prairie (Coleman/Ames), both pieces split this run from T-2919 and T-2984, read against the 1888 Inland Architect plate through its solved camera.

## T-2987: the bay rock-faced to its sill course, smooth above, and the plate's two downpipes
*(piece 1 of T-2919)*

- **Dressing.** On the plate the north bay is rock-faced in large courses up to its first floor's sill course (about y 575–580 px) and smooth ashlar above, like the oriel. Before this, the build's bay walls were flat all the way up. K08's rock-faced relief (`masonry`) can now stop at one of a bay's storey lines (`masonry.to_m`, new and validated against the bay's own storeys). 1811's bay carries it on its basement and ground storeys, and its first floor stands smooth over the 5.0 m band. Courses are 0.6 m and blocks about 1.1 m (the plate's are about 30 × 45–55 px at 47.4 px/m).
- **Downpipes.** The plate draws two on the front: one beside the bay's south return (a pale rod at x 298–302 px, clear of the tree's trunk) and one down the entrance block's south corner (x 505–510 px) to a shoe at grade. A gable K01 roof used to refuse any rainwater. It may now carry T-2953's `front_pipes` alone, each from a rainwater head of its own, with no eave gutter. The pipes are built at 5.7 m and 10.25 m from the north corner and render at x ≈ 296 and ≈ 500 px.
- The rainwater block stays `reconstructed`: the pipes' places are read, but their fabric, paint, heads and straps are K04's. It is recorded in L-k01-1811-ames-front-2541.

## T-2990: the stair cheeks' scrolls on foot blocks
*(piece 1 of T-2984)*

- On the plate each cheek's roll stands on a plain block (south cheek x 421–440 px), with its centre about 0.9 m over grade. K07's scrolled cheek learns `foot_block_m` (record: `cheek_form: {kind: scrolled, foot_block_m: 0.7}`). The roll now lands at y 773–790 px against the plate's 775–792, where before it sat on grade.

## Split off, with their readings (not built here)
- **T-2988**: the bay's canted north face. K08's projection is square-cornered, and K01 refuses an asymmetric bay plan.
- **T-2989**: the oriel. The plate's is a flat-fronted box about 3 m across on square returns, with a multi-light south return, a rounded rock-faced base, and its cornice under the eave datum.
- **T-2991**: the porch's south arcade. Its capitals and crowns step down across x 476–501, so it stands on a face receding at about v 9.4–9.5. That disagrees with the solve's south corner (v 10.40, x 510), and the oriel's return points the same way, so the entrance block's south corner needs a re-read first.

data.body:
## T-2982 — the district's named context buildings, drafted (piece 1 of T-2162)

T-2162 (the district's edges) was split along its own bound, into exactly two pieces. This PR is piece 1. T-2983, the background census, is piece 2.

### What a visitor sees
- **Second Presbyterian Church** at Michigan and 20th: the nave, the parish hall across the west end and the north aisle. Its south-east tower carries **the full spire it had in 1904**, which the 1901 Tribune cut and Sloan's photograph show; the spire was lost in 1929.
- **213, 215 and 217 East Twentieth Street**: three brick rowhouses. 217 has its street gable and a turret at its Prairie corner.
- **2008 Calumet, Hanford**: a steep brownstone hip with stone faces on its front and south side. **2018 Calumet, Wheeler-Kohn**: a mansard. Each has its brick barn on the alley.

### How
- **The five houses.** These were read off Sanborn sheet 35 into a census of their own (`data/components/prairie_1904/edges_census_s35.json`), because the T-1842 census counts Prairie frontages only and its checker holds the census directory to Prairie ranges. The T-2340 tracer reads them as sheet `35x`; sheets 20, 28 and 35 re-derive byte for byte. The draft builder now names a building by the street its lot faces, a row may name its body's trace part (`main_part`) and its own rear ticket, and a feature may take an explicit `at_m`. All 118 earlier draft records are unchanged (`--check`).
- **The church.** No committed sheet reaches Michigan, so it is a new `sites` row. Its plan comes from **HABS IL-328** sheet 2, read at the feet bar: the metric bar disagrees by 22 %, and the pews' 0.92 m spacing settles which is right. Its heights come from sheet 4's printed levels (the hall's gable 80'-1", the nave's ridge 87'-8 1/4"). The tower's 38 m of masonry and 16 m spire are proportions read off Sloan's photograph. The position is **reconstructed**, good to a few metres: Michigan's terrain-box line moved in by a 66 ft half-width, and 20th Street's measured north line, each with a 3 m setback.
